title: Secure logout
idea: A secure logout ends the session in two places: it deletes the stored refresh token on the server and clears both cookies in the browser.
points: Logout is a `POST` route behind `verifyJWT`, so `req.user` already identifies the caller.
`$unset` deletes the stored `refreshToken`, so a copied refresh token stops matching.
`clearCookie` needs the options used to set the cookie, minus `maxAge` and `expires`.
The access token is stateless, so it stays valid until its short expiry.

hero.title: What logout has to undo

left.title: Clear the cookies only
items: The database still holds the refresh token.
A copied refresh token keeps working until it expires.

right.title: Clear the cookies and the stored token
items: `clearCookie` expires both cookies in the browser.
A copied refresh token no longer matches the stored one.
The access token lives on until its short expiry.

hero.verdict: Logout ends the refresh path at once; the access token expires on its own.

walk.text: A demo secret; real ones live in `.env`.
Stand-ins for earlier files: utils, a trimmed `User` and `verifyJWT`.
The server half: `$unset` deletes `refreshToken` from the user document.
Use the same options as login: `httpOnly`, and `secure` in production.
Clear both cookies, then reply. The browser receives two already-expired cookies.
A secured `POST` route: `verifyJWT` runs first, so `req.user` is set.
Log out, then inspect: two clearing headers, no stored token, access token still accepted.

pitfalls: Clearing only the cookies leaves a copied refresh token working until it expires.
Give `clearCookie` the same options as `res.cookie`, or browsers keep the cookie.
Expect `401` from `/logout` once the access token has expired: refresh first.

quiz.why: Logout changed only the database and the browser's cookies. The access token still verifies until it expires.

takeaway: Revoke the refresh token on the server; let the short access token expire.
